newsitem.title: USA: Reebok sues Sony's Tristar over film.
newsitem.headline: Reebok sues Sony's Tristar over film.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd said it filed a lawsuit against Sony Corp's Tristar Pictures Inc, seeking up to $110 million in damages for violating a product placement agreement in the movie, "Jerry Maguire."

"The suit minimally seeks $10 million for trademark disparagement," said a Reebok spokesman who said Sony violated an agreement by deleting an uplifting Reebok commercial that was supposed to be part of the film's ending, but left an earlier negative reference to Reebok, using an expletive.
Tristar and Sony officials were unavailable for comment.
The film stars Tom Cruise as a sports agent with just one client, a football star who yearns for greater recognition and an endorsement by Reebok.

"The whole premise of our participation was predicated on the fact the movie's main character transforms himself...and comes full circle, achieving his professional dream and getting a big deal with Reebok."
Reebok said it spent a total of $1.5 million providing products for the film and producing the commercial. It also said it prepared a multimillion dollar promotional package for the film.
"We invested a lot and all this was predicated on the product placement agreement we had, which included the commercial at the end," the spokesman said.
